source.title: The Resistance to Label Noise in K-NN and DNN Depends on its Concentration
source.authors: Amnon Drory; Oria Ratzon; S. Avidan; R. Giryes

page_placements.theme: Corruption structure matters beyond its rate

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the complete paper and appendix; the paper is followed by a duplicated, separately formatted appendix. No material relevant to the reported results appears cut off.
record.tranche_reason: The study trains networks on varying types and levels of label corruption and measures clean-test accuracy. This bears directly on label-noise robustness, but it does not test fitting completely random labels, training error, time-to-fit, unstructured inputs, regularization removal, or learning order.
record.gate_note: The study reports results from its own noisy-label training experiments. Figure values are not stated numerically in text; rows relying on those curves retain figure-only values. Its reported K-NN analyses and prior-work summaries are not counted as DNN result rows. Softmax/K-NN similarity is a separate reported measurement and does not directly measure any listed version.
record.test_reason: The study measures clean-test accuracy as randomly spread label corruption increases, testing the generalization component of V4. Clean-validation early stopping deliberately reduces memorization; noisy-label training fit is not reported.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that noise concentration governs robustness and that their K-NN analysis provides a first-order approximation to DNN test accuracy. Effective K varies across experiments and remains unresolved.
record.recipe_differences: This study varies label-noise type and level and measures clean-test accuracy, rather than assigning completely random labels and assessing training fit and chance test error. It uses early stopping for MNIST and CIFAR-10; ImageNet uses Adam and early stopping.
record.method_sensitivity: Noise type and level; locally concentrated noise is harder than uniform or flip noise. The authors state that resistance in flip noise holds only until noise approaches 50%, while uniform-noise accuracy drops noticeably only near 90%.

fits_no_version.finding: Locally concentrated corruption causes substantially greater test-accuracy degradation: the MNIST illustration reports approximately 80% accuracy with 20% concentrated noise versus approximately 100% with randomly spread noise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: DNN resistance to label noise depends on whether corruption is randomly spread or concentrated in feature-space regions.

fits_no_version.finding: The median chi-square distance between softmax outputs and locally selected K-NN histograms is 0.143123, after selecting K separately for each example.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Softmax outputs can resemble local training-label distributions in a learned embedding.

record.problems: Accuracy curves are presented in figures without numerical values in the text. The main reported DNN accuracy measure is on a clean test set; training error under noise is not reported. The authors note deviations between experimental and analytical curves and say the effective K changes between experiments. The text does not state the number of repeats for ImageNet.
record.rows_left_out: No DNN accuracy result rows were omitted. K-NN analytical and experimental accuracy results are not DNN results and were not extracted as rows for this claim. Prior-work results mentioned in Related Work were excluded.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training error on fully random labels with unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Time to fit random versus real labels and convergence speed as corruption increases.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit throughout the corruption sweep and simultaneous memorization of noise. Exact curve values and the fully random-label chance endpoint are unavailable in the supplied text.
Necessity or sufficiency of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation.
Temporal ordering of learning real patterns and memorizing noise. Early stopping is motivated by cited work, without an independent trajectory test.

missing.what: ImageNet DenseNet-121 clean-test accuracy under randomly spread flip noise is omitted despite the statement that no DNN accuracy rows were omitted.
missing.versions: V4, as a corruption-mechanism scope comparison

missing.what: MNIST clean-test accuracy under a general corruption matrix is omitted. Record its conditions and recoverable qualitative result without inventing numerical values.
missing.versions: V4, as a corruption-mechanism scope comparison

record.verdict_notes: Observed states for uniform-noise rows refer to the measured generalization component, not verified memorization. Missing training-fit measurements are untested, not evidence against fitting random labels. Concentrated corruption does not warrant a V4 scope verdict because it changes the random-selection condition.

versions.untested_parts: No experiment uses completely random labels or reports training error, chance test error, or unchanged hyperparameters for fitting random labels.
No training-time comparison or convergence-speed result is reported.
No shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise inputs are tested.

Tests uniform and flip noise, plus locally concentrated noise, but does not test a single sweep from none to all corrupted labels with perfect training fit throughout; the paper reports clean-test accuracy curves, not training error.
Does not compare regularization, dropout, or augmentation settings or test their necessity or sufficiency.
No training trajectory or evidence about whether clean patterns are learned before noisy labels is reported.

rows.subject: MNIST DNN inspired by LENET-5 and AlexNet
rows.operation_detail: Retrained on MNIST with uniformly random label noise at varying noise levels; evaluated on the clean test set.
rows.note: The text says the DNN experiments were repeated 10 times for MNIST and that experimental curves show mean accuracy and standard deviation. The figure's curve is described as noise resistance, but exact values are not stated.

relationships.condition: Uniform random corruption; MNIST, CIFAR-10, and ImageNet; early-stopped training
relationships.reason: R1, R3, and R5 support retention of signal under substantial random corruption and degradation at high corruption; Section 4 places noticeable accuracy loss near 90%. This supports the generalization component only.
relationships.display_finding: Predictive signal persisted under substantial corruption, with noticeable accuracy loss emerging near 90% corruption.

relationships.display_finding: A transition occurred near 50% corruption, after which networks learned the alternative labels instead of approaching chance predictions.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: uniform noise on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and ImageNet, and flip noise on MNIST and CIFAR-10
reader_labels.reason: The authors report that the experimental curves follow the predicted behavior; for uniform noise, accuracy drops noticeably only near 90%, and for flip noise resistance holds until noise approaches 50% (R1–R5). The plotted values are not transcribed numerically.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: locally concentrated noise on MNIST and CIFAR-10
reader_labels.reason: The authors report that the networks do not overcome locally concentrated noise and predict no resistance, while figure-only curves do not establish perfect training fit or a full test-error progression (R6–R7).
